newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks whipsawed by poll rumours, end lower.
newsitem.headline: French stocks whipsawed by poll rumours, end lower.

text.p: The Paris bourse closed with narrow losses on Thursday, after losing earlier gains in a busy session marked by conflicting rumours over private opinion polls on Sunday's parliamentary runoff vote.
"I do not even try to understand anymore, there are really no targets either up or down, it's purely reacting to rumours," a broker said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 3.93 points or 0.15 percent at 2,579.24, while the CAC-40 May futures contract was down three at 2,576 from Wednesday's close.
Volume was a heavy 10.69 billion francs.

Market talk of a private poll putting the Socialists ahead of the conservative parties deflated an earlier rise of 1.72 percent, which had been based on a rumour of an opinion poll putting right-wing parties ahead.
"It's a market of excesses. There have been enormous swings but they do not mean much. On top of that, the dollar is up and the international situation is not bad," a broker said.
Thursday marked the second consecutive session closing below the psychologically important 2,600 level. Non-domestic investors were said to be the main sellers.
The market was also worried by the row between the German government and the Bundesbank over a revalutation of gold reserves in a bid to plug public deficits, traders said.
Gan adds four percent to 130 francs, helped by Fortis and Allianz statements of interest in the insurer.
Sommer Allibert drops 9.85 percent to 189.50 on news it is buying Germany's Tarkett, which will double its debt.
Two blocks of Scor shares change hands. The reinsurer closes down 2.11 percent at 231.5.
Navigation Mixte share buy-in to start on Friday and run to June 30. The stock ended unchanged at 871.
